s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden collapse with ventricular fibrillation and subsequent coma
key_facts: 21-year-old woman with autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability
On risperidone
No prior history of syncope, cardiac arrest, or known cardiovascular disease
Family denied any illicit drug or alcohol use
Witnessed collapse at a noisy auto mechanic shop
Ventricular fibrillation on bystander ECG
Return of spontaneous circulation after two defibrillations
Blood pressure 93/70 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, and oxygen saturation 100% on arrival
Intravenous amiodarone infusion and oral amiodarone administered
Comatose state with agonal respirations on examination
Normal chemistry panel and electrolytes
Initial electrocardiogram showed sinus rhythm with interpolated premature ventricular complexes and a QTc of 380 ms
Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated an ejection fraction of 45-50%, normal wall thickness, and no valvular abnormalities

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Witnessed collapse with ventricular fibrillation and subsequent coma, normal heart structure on echocardiogram

shortlist.label: Risperidone-induced QT prolongation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient on risperidone, which can cause QT prolongation and increase risk of ventricular fibrillation

shortlist.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: No clear cardiac abnormality found on examination or testing, but ventricular fibrillation occurred

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Ventricular fibrillation and reduced ejection fraction, possible right ventricular involvement

shortlist.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Reduced ejection fraction and normal wall thickness on echocardiogram, possible dilated cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's witnessed collapse, ventricular fibrillation, and normal cardiac structure on echocardiography, combined with the presence of premature ventricular complexes on the electrocardiogram, are consistent with this diagnosis. The trigger of a noisy environment also fits with the condition's known triggers.

rejected.label: Risperidone-induced QT prolongation
rejected.why: The QTc interval was 380 ms, which is not significantly prolonged to explain the ventricular fibrillation.

rejected.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
rejected.why: While possible, this diagnosis does not provide a specific mechanism or underlying cause for the ventricular fibrillation, making it less preferable to CPVT, which has a clearer pathophysiological basis.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The echocardiogram did not show any evidence of right ventricular dysfunction or structural abnormalities typical of ARVC.

rejected.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The ejection fraction was reduced but not severely so, and the wall thickness was normal, which does not strongly support a diagnosis of dilated cardiomyopathy as the primary cause of the ventricular fibrillation.
